Two of the world's most powerful institutions just made the same admission about AI — in the same week.

The European Commission detailed new Digital Markets Act requirements on July 16 that would force Google to open its AI capabilities to competitors through interoperability mandates. Just days earlier, the US Federal Reserve stood up a dedicated AI task force under Marc Andreessen, essentially acknowledging that AI is reshaping economic fundamentals faster than existing models can explain.

For business leaders, this is not abstract policy. It is a direct signal that the era of building your AI strategy inside one platform's walled garden has an expiration date. If interoperability is mandated, every tight integration you built with a single AI provider becomes a liability that needs re-architecture — and that re-architecture happens on a regulatory timeline, not yours.

The economic picture is equally telling: strong productivity numbers, declining white-collar hiring, and an infrastructure investment boom running on strained power grids. Central banks cannot fully explain what is happening. That uncertainty creates both risk and opportunity for companies positioned to move quickly.

The strategic move right now is building platform-agnostic AI architectures that give your organization optionality regardless of which direction regulation turns.
